Source: http://www.marijuananews.com

Posted May 8, 2000
Analysis by Richard Cowan
See
The Marijuana Resistance Movement
Beyond Reform: From Ideas To Action.
Analysis By Richard Cowan

Frankly, I hate rallies and marches. Lord knows I have been to enough of them, Saturday in Vancouver being the most recent, but I go out of sense of duty.
See
Rolling Stone Corporate Sponsor of Greenwich Village " Family Day " -
Bumps Marijuana March, Times Are A’Changing

Consequently, when the idea of the Millenium Marijuana March first surfaced I was not very enthusiastic.

I was wrong.

The war on marijuana has begun to choke on its own excesses. The marches themselves can dramatize this, just as the violence against civil rights marchers in Selma once showed the world the cruelty of segregation. In New York, almost uniquely among the events in large cities, there were over 300 arrests. This highlights the fact that under Mayor Giuliani there were nearly 47 times as many marijuana arrests last year (33,471) as in 1992 (720). This cannot continue.
See
New York Times Reports The Numbers In City’s Soaring Marijuana Arrests:
A Journalistic Breakthrough?

There have been so many arrests, so many lies, and so much injustice, that the backlash has finally begun, and it is moving toward critical mass.

The Internet has accelerated the process by allowing people to communicate with their allies and coordinate events on a scale not seen since the Vietnam War.

Saturday’s marches in perhaps 100 cities around the world manifested a global resistance to marijuana prohibition that observers of the political process should no longer ignore.

What I have called the Marijuana Resistance Movement is now on the world stage.

These " facts on the ground " present the prohibitionist media with a real challenge. The Washington Post did not deign to tell its readers about either the DC march to the Capitol or about any of the other marches.
See
How The Washington Post Tells Its Readers
About The House of Lords Report On Medical Marijuana -- With Great Subtlety!
and
Washington PostFinally Reports On Bizarro’s Dutch Fiasco;
No Mention of Murder Rates – More Fact-Free Journalism
and
How Does the Washington Post Tell Its Readers About New German Government’s Marijuana Policy?
Very Carefully.

This is a form of self-censorship that is deceiving the very people who most need to know this, the DEAland politicians. Sometimes silence can be the biggest lie of all.

As of Monday night, the wire services are yet to assemble reports from their bureaus around the world and do what they are best equipped to do in reporting on a global event.
(If you want to find stories on many of the marches see www.mapinc.org )

I usually object when a marijuana reform organization or event is called " pro-marijuana " because they would be more accurately described as " opposed to marijuana prohibition. " In fact, many of the opponents of marijuana prohibition are also opposed to the use of marijuana, or are at least not interested in it.

(Of course, the prohibitionist media cannot use the term " marijuana prohibition, " lest the current policy be linked in the public mind with (alcohol) Prohibition, which is generally recognized as a disaster. Try writing to your local paper, and ask them why they never use the term. It would be interesting to see if they can be jarred into consciousness. The widespread use of the words " marijuana prohibition " will be a real milestone on the road to freedom.)

However, in all candor, these marches really are " pro-marijuana " and the cannabis leaf has become a universally recognized symbol that the prohibitionists love to hate. The prohibitionists have only themselves to blame for this. If it were not for marijuana prohibition, the leaf would not be a political symbol and there would be no occasion for " pro-marijuana " events on such a scale.

And notice that there are no " pro-cocaine, " or " pro-heroin, " or even " pro-psychedelic " marches. There may be some vocal opposition to other aspects of the " drug war, " but there is no large-scale politicized constituency for any other " drug. " That is something that the political analysts need to understand.

In Praise of Marijuana.

The medical marijuana movement has contributed greatly to creating much of the unapologetically " pro-marijuana " aspect of the marijuana resistance movement. For the patients, marijuana really is a positive good in their lives. However, marijuana is also a positive good in the lives of people whose use would not meet the standard definitions of " medical. " For example, consider the comments of the late Carl Sagan.
See
At Dinner With Carl Sagan the Only Drug Was Wine, But That Is Not News.

As more and more people who do not like marijuana join the opposition to marijuana prohibition they may be discomfited by those who are " pro-marijuana " – but as one protestor in Vancouver said Saturday, " We’re here. We’re high. Get used to it. "

Obviously, this was an echo of the once radical gay rights slogan, " We’re here. We’re queer. Etc. " And the message is the same: People have a right to be who they are. One may be turned off by, or even morally opposed to, marijuana use or homoeroticism, or baptisms, but one can still respect the rights of others to be who they are.

I have said again and again, that the real reason that marijuana is illegal is not because of what the prohibitionists do, as powerful as they are, but rather because of what marijuana users do not do. Not enough of us stand up for our rights. Clearly, this is changing, and the issue is not going to go away.

Marijuana prohibition is going to end. The only questions are how soon, how many lives will be ruined, and how much more damage will be done to the polity before it happens?

Prohibitionists will naturally view this as a threat. But those who need to understand this most are the anti-prohibitionists who still cannot grasp the importance of the issue, and are reluctant to take it seriously and give it a place on the public agenda.
See
Ottawa Citizen Practices First Class Journalism
A Brilliantly Insightful Editorial: " Marijuana isn’t just a serious issue. It’s huge. "

There will be more marches next year and they will be both bigger and better. The Internet is just coming into its own as a political organizing tool. It will have both a quantitative and qualitative impact on these events.

This year, thanks to Marc Emory, Pot-TV.net covered marches around the world for the first time. We are very new at this, but as we learn the creative use of the Internet, combined with street theatre, the events will become a form of " infotainment " and a great educational and mobilizing tool. The marijuana resistance movement is here, it's growing, get used to it!

Better yet, become a part of it. As Shakespeare said, all the world’s a stage, and now we are writing the play.

Be sure and log on to www.pot-tv.net for the 420 MarijuanaNews with Richard Cowan weekdays at 4:20PM and again at 7:00PM Pacific time.
